chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said:

I said to Zurara: Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Women do not inherit from what their husband leaves of the ground of a house or land, unless the structure, trunks, and wood are valued, so she is given her share from the value of the structure. As for the ground, she is given nothing of the land, nor the ground of the house.' Zurara said: There is no doubt about this.
ai.seo_question: Do women inherit the land or just the structure in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from Zurara, a key figure in Shia jurisprudence, clarifies the distinction between land (turba) and the built structure (building materials) in inheritance, establishing that women inherit the value of the construction but not the ground itself. This ruling reflects the Shia interpretation of how fixed assets are valued and distributed, emphasizing that the physical land remains distinct from the improvements upon it. The hadith underscores the precision of early Shia scholars in differentiating between tangible property types to ensure equitable distribution among heirs.
